items.title: ONE token turned a $0.40 AI request into $0.80.
items.summary:
ONE token turned a $0.40 AI request into $0.80.

and 4 "cheap" $20 subscriptions quietly cost $1,080 a year.

so i wrote 98 lines of python to audit what AI actually costs. real published prices, no vibes.

it said cut $360. the cache line alone was -88%.

here's what nobody checks.

ChatGPT Plus $20. Claude Pro $20. SuperGrok $30. Cursor Pro $20.
$90 a month. $1,080 a year. before tax.

each one looks reasonable the day you click subscribe. the bill only shows up when they stack

what the script printed, prices as of Aug 28, US web:

> 5M input + 1M output tokens a month: Sonnet 5 $20.00, Grok 4.6 $16.00, GPT-5.6 Luna $2.20
> use 1/5 of that and Sonnet is $4. not $20
> keep 2 subs + a $20 API budget: $720/yr. saves $360
> agent sending the same 100K prompt 50 times: $10.00 naive, $1.23 cached. -88%
> batch API: half price if you can wait
> Grok 4.6 at 199,999 tokens: $0.40. at 200,000: $0.80. one token doubles the whole request
> 20K records to JSON: $160 on Sol, $8.80 on Luna (my assumption: 1K in / 200 out each)

the lesson isn't "API is cheaper". heavy users burn $20 of API in days. the lesson is most people never did the math

how to audit yours:
1. list every AI sub and what you actually use it for
2. split the product (IDE, bots, connectors) from the model access
3. log 30 days of how often you open each one
4. move the occasional ones to pay-per-token
5. cache stable prompts, batch what can wait, watch the 200K / 272K cliffs
6. route easy work to cheap models, keep the frontier one for hard problems

every subscription has to earn its spot on your card. my math on published prices, not financial advice

i won't say anything more:

results.input: Bạn là gì và làm được những gì?

result.actual_text:
Tôi là **Gemini**, một mô hình ngôn ngữ lớn được phát triển bởi **Google**.

Tôi được huấn luyện để hiểu và xử lý ngôn ngữ tự nhiên, đóng vai trò như một trợ lý ảo hỗ trợ bạn trong nhiều công việc khác nhau. Dưới đây là những khả năng chính của tôi:

### 1. Xử lý & Tạo nội dung văn bản
* **Viết lách:** Soạn thảo email, bài viết, báo cáo, bài luận, thơ, kịch bản, nội dung tiếp thị...
* **Tóm tắt & phân tích:** Đọc hiểu và rút gọn các văn bản dài, bài báo nghiên cứu hoặc tài liệu phức tạp.
* **Biên tập:** Sửa lỗi chính tả, ngữ pháp, viết lại câu theo phong cách hoặc giọng điệu mong muốn.
* **Dịch thuật:** Hỗ trợ chuyển đổi giữa nhiều ngôn ngữ với ngữ cảnh tự nhiên.

### 2. Lập trình & Kỹ thuật
* Viết, sửa lỗi (debug) và tối ưu hóa mã nguồn trong nhiều ngôn ngữ lập trình (Python, JavaScript, C++, Go, Java, v.v.).
* Hướng dẫn giải thuật, thiết kế cấu trúc dữ liệu, viết truy vấn SQL.
* Giải thích các khái niệm kỹ thuật và kiến trúc hệ thống.

### 3. Học tập, Nghiên cứu & Giải quyết vấn đề
* Giải thích các khái niệm phức tạp từ khoa học, toán học, kinh tế đến lịch sử, văn hóa.
* Hỗ trợ tìm kiếm, tổng hợp tài liệu khoa học và thông tin mới.
* Phân tích logic, giải toán và tư duy suy luận từng bước.

### 4. Lên kế hoạch & Tổ chức công việc
* Lập kế hoạch học tập, lịch trình làm việc, kế hoạch du lịch.
* Động não (brainstorming) ý tưởng cho dự án, sản phẩm hoặc sự kiện mới.

Bạn đang cần hỗ trợ về chủ đề hay công việc cụ thể nào? Hãy cho tôi biết nhé!

items.title: From TractEasy to TLD Robotics: A new chapter in autonomous airport operations - Robotics & Automation News
items.summary: # From TractEasy to TLD Robotics: A new chapter in autonomous airport operations. **After almost a decade of collaboration, the companies behind one of the more established autonomous vehicle programs in airport ground operations have brought their activities together under a single name: TLD Robotics.**. The new company was formally launched in September 2026, following ALVEST Group’s acquisition of autonomous driving technology developer EasyMile. Bringing together EasyMile, TractEasy and TLD’s existing driverless vehicle activities, TLD Robotics represents a consolidation of technology, manufacturing and operational expertise that has been developing since 2017. It reflects a broader change in the autonomous vehicle industry, particularly in airports, logistics facilities and industrial environments, where the emphasis is gradually shifting from demonstrating autonomous technology to making it a dependable part of everyday operations. For TLD Robotics, that transition has been nearly a decade in the making. The collaboration between TLD and EasyMile sought to address these challenges by combining autonomous driving software with purpose-built industrial vehicles.

items.title: Opinion: Supervised autonomy in robotics starts with the robot’s worst day - Robotics & Automation News
items.summary: # Opinion: Supervised autonomy in robotics starts with the robot’s worst day. **Supervised autonomy in robotics is usually described from the robot’s side: the machine does the repetitive work, and a person steps in when something goes wrong.**. The harder design question sits on the human side, and many projects leave it until commissioning, when nobody has yet agreed who answers the robot when it gets stuck. In a recent interview with Sam Francis for *Robotics & Automation News*, Plus One Robotics chief executive Erik Nieves argued that a robot should be judged on its worst day: how it behaves in front of something it has never encountered, rather than on a smooth demonstration. If today’s AI still struggles to recognise the limits of its own competence, as Nieves put it, then the human backstop has to be engineered with the same care as the gripper and the conveyor.

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: Setting a new standard for responsible AI infrastructure | OpenAI
items.summary: The promise of AI is that it gives people more power to shape their own futures. It can help someone learn a new skill, build a business, or solve a problem that was previously out of reach. Building more computing infrastructure capacity in the United States can help lower the cost of delivering AI, put these tools in more people’s hands, and ensure America stays at the forefront of the technology. [...] protect residents, and ensure that the benefits of AI infrastructure are broadly shared. We’ll also make sustained investments in priorities residents help select.

items.title: OpenAI to pay for data center power after election shows AI concern
items.summary: OpenAI reaffirmed its promise to pay the full cost of powering data centers as part of a series of commitments the company published Thursday, two days after voters at the polls roundly rejected the rapid expansion of AI. [...] AI companies like OpenAI depend on AI data centers to serve customers and develop new models, and they're seeking to build out as rapidly as possible to meet demand. In February, OpenAI told investors that it's targeting $600 billion in total compute spend by 2030, and the company has since announced massive data center projects in Georgia and Ohio. [...] OpenAI has repeatedly pledged to protect ratepayers and invest in local communities this year, and Lehane said the company's latest commitments build on many of its previous initiatives. He said the policy blueprint has been in the works since August, and that he met with dozens of lawmakers and candidates since then.

OpenAI and Anthropic have tried to ​maintain a more open research culture to both ⁠attract employees and foster creativity that can lead to breakthroughs. The AI field is rooted in academia, where machine-learning scientists have openly discussed their research.
